review_notes: I read the whole target file and the definitions in PlanarConjugacy.lean (map, box, instruction, box_halfWidth, instruction_conjugacy). I grepped for simp attributes there and found none on map or box. I cannot run Lean, so the claims below concern the structure of the simp interface and the repeated proof patterns, not observed simp behaviour. I did not examine the other files that use these declarations in detail. I found no rewrite cycles and no competing simp rules in this file.

findings.declaration: PlanarConjugacy.map / Planar.coordinateMap (component evaluation interface, used in initialPoint_spec, coordinateMap_bounds, step_realized)
findings.excerpt:
simp only [coordinateMap, PlanarConjugacy.map, shift, Matrix.cons_val_zero,
    Matrix.cons_val_one, Rat.cast_sub, Rat.cast_mul, Rat.cast_div, Rat.cast_ofNat]
findings.problem: `PlanarConjugacy.map` is a `![_, _]` vector definition with no component simp lemmas such as `map a b ε c x 0 = a + ε * x 1` and `map a b ε c x 1 = b - c * x 0`. `Planar.coordinateMap` has none either. Every consumer therefore unfolds `map`, then `coordinateMap`, then `shift`, and then rewrites with `Matrix.cons_val_*` and a hand-picked list of `Rat.cast_*` lemmas. The same unfolding recurs at line 64 (`simp [initialPoint, PlanarConjugacy.map]`, an unrestricted simp after `fin_cases`), at lines 123–124 (`instruction_halfWidths`), and at lines 139–140. `point_second` instead uses `change` plus `norm_num only` at lines 190–191. These ad-hoc lists differ from one proof to the next, and they expand `shift` and `compression` as well as `map`.
findings.proposed_change: In PlanarConjugacy.lean, add `@[simp] theorem map_apply_zero (a b ε c : ℚ) (x : Plane) : map a b ε c x 0 = (b : ℝ) - c * x 0`, with the correct components, and `map_apply_one` in the same way. Both can be proved by `rfl`, or by `simp [map]`. In this file, add `coordinateMap_apply_zero` and `coordinateMap_apply_one` as simp lemmas, stated with `shift` and `compression` kept folded. Then `point_second` and `coordinateMap_bounds` become `simp only [coordinateMap_apply_zero, coordinateMap_apply_one]` followed by arithmetic. `initialPoint_spec` no longer needs an open-ended `simp [... PlanarConjugacy.map]`.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical normal form for evaluating the coordinate change. Proofs stop repeating a fragile unfolding list. `shift` and `compression` stay folded, so their definitions are not expanded unnecessarily.

findings.declaration: Planar.instruction (and PlanarConjugacy.instruction / box) unfolding interface; instruction_source_separation, instruction_target_separation, instruction_source_bounds, instruction_target_bounds
findings.problem: `Planar.instruction` is defined as `PlanarConjugacy.instruction ...`, which in turn is a structure literal `⟨box .., box .., factor⁻¹⟩`. There are no simp or rfl-lemmas stating `(instruction M hM b).source = PlanarConjugacy.box (shift M hM) (43/128) (compression M hM) (11/32) (geometricInstruction M hM b).source`, and none for `.target`. The proofs instead use `change ... (PlanarConjugacy.box _ _ _ _ _).carrier` with five underscore arguments. This recurs at lines 95, 105, 147 and 156, and `instruction_halfWidths` at lines 123–124 needs `simp only [instruction, PlanarConjugacy.instruction, ...]`. The `change` calls rely on defeq unification of the underscores, so they are fragile. A reader cannot use `simp` or `rw` to move between the instruction and its boxes.
findings.proposed_change: Add `theorem instruction_source (M hM b) : (instruction M hM b).source = PlanarConjugacy.box (shift M hM) (43/128) (compression M hM) (11/32) (geometricInstruction M hM b).source := rfl`, and `instruction_target` in the same way. Mark both `@[simp]` only if the boxes are the preferred normal form. Otherwise use them with `rw`, and let `instruction_halfWidths` use `simp only [instruction_source, instruction_target]`. Also add `PlanarConjugacy.instruction_source/target/factor` projection lemmas, in PlanarConjugacy.lean, for the structure literal. The four `change` lines then become `rw [instruction_source, instruction_source]` or `simp only [instruction_source]`.
findings.benefit: The unfolding of `instruction` goes through a documented rewrite rule, not repeated `change _ _ _ _ _` patterns. The proofs no longer depend on unification of underscores. The projections of `instruction` then reduce to `box`, which already has `box_halfWidth` and `box_center`.
